translation_en: Yahya ibn Bukayr narrated to us: Al-Layth narrated to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, who said: ‘Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyib, ‘Alqamah ibn Waqqas, and ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Utbah ibn Mas‘ud informed me, reporting from the account of ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, concerning what the people of the slander said about her and how Allah declared her innocent of what they said. Each of them narrated a portion of the account to me; the accounts of some confirm those of the others, although some remembered it more fully than others. The account ‘Urwah narrated to me from ‘A’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, is this: ‘A’ishah, the wife of the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: Whenever the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, wanted to set out on a journey, he would draw lots among his wives. Whichever wife’s lot came out, he would take her with him. ‘A’ishah said: He drew lots among us for one of the expeditions he undertook, and my lot came out. I went with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, after the command for hijab had been revealed. I was carried in my howdah and lowered in it. We traveled until the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had finished that expedition and was returning. As we drew near Madinah on our way back, he announced one night that we would depart. I got up when they announced the departure and walked until I had gone beyond the army. When I had finished what I needed to do, I returned to my riding place and found that my necklace of Zafar beads had broken. I went looking for it, and searching for it delayed me. The group of men who used to carry my howdah came and lifted it, placed it on my camel, which I had been riding, and set it on the camel. They thought I was inside it. At that time women were light in weight, for flesh had not made them heavy; they ate only a little food. So the people did not notice how light the howdah was when they lifted it. I was a young girl, and they sent the camel on its way and departed. I found my necklace after the army had moved on. I came to their stopping place, but there was no caller and no one answering. I made for the place where I had been staying, thinking that they would notice I was missing and come back for me. While I sat there, sleep overcame me and I fell asleep. Safwan ibn al-Mu‘attal al-Sulami, then al-Dhakwani, had been behind the army. He traveled during the night and reached my stopping place in the morning. He saw the dark outline of a sleeping person, came to me, and recognized me when he saw me, for he had seen me before the command for hijab. I woke when he said, “We belong to Allah and to Him we return,” upon recognizing me. I covered my face with my outer garment. By Allah, he did not say a word to me, nor did I hear any word from him other than that remembrance. He made his riding camel kneel, stepped on its forelegs, and I mounted it. He then led the camel by its reins until we reached the army, after they had stopped in the heat of midday. Those who were destined to perish perished, and the one who took the leading role in the slander was ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul. We arrived in Madinah, and I fell ill when we arrived. I was ill for a month while people were spreading the talk of those who had made the slander, and I knew nothing of it. What made me uneasy during my illness was that I did not see from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the kindness I used to see from him when I was ill. He would come in, greet me, and ask, “How is that woman?” Then he would leave. That made me uneasy, but I knew nothing of what was happening until I had recovered and went out. Umm Mistah went out with me toward al-Manasi‘, our place for relieving ourselves. We used to go out only at night, before we made latrines near our houses. We followed the old Arab custom of going out to the open ground to relieve ourselves, and we disliked making latrines beside our houses. I went with Umm Mistah. She was the daughter of Abu Ruhm ibn ‘Abd Manaf; her mother was the daughter of Sakhr ibn ‘Amir, the maternal aunt of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq. Her son was Mistah ibn Uthathah. As Umm Mistah and I were returning toward my house, after finishing what we needed to do, Umm Mistah tripped over her cloak and said, “May Mistah be ruined!” I said to her, “How bad is what you have said! Are you insulting a man who was present at Badr?” She said, “You poor thing, have you not heard what he said?” I asked, “What did he say?” She told me what the people of the slander were saying, and my illness grew worse. When I returned home, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, came in—meaning, he greeted me—and asked, “How is that woman?” I said, “Will you give me permission to go to my parents?” At that time I wanted to make sure of the report from them. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, gave me permission, and I went to my parents. I said to my mother, “Mother, what are people talking about?” She said, “My daughter, take it easy. By Allah, it is rare for a beautiful woman who is loved by her husband and has co-wives not to have them speak much against her.” I said, “Glory be to Allah! Have people really been talking about this?” I wept that night until morning; my tears would not stop, and I could not sleep. In the morning, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, called ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib and Usamah ibn Zayd, may Allah be pleased with them both, when revelation had been delayed, to consult them about separating from his wife. Usamah advised the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, based on what he knew of his family’s innocence and the affection he knew the Prophet had for them. He said, “Messenger of Allah, she is your wife, and we know nothing but good of her.” As for ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib, he said, “Messenger of Allah, Allah has not restricted you; there are many women besides her. If you ask the servant girl, she will tell you the truth.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, called for Barirah and said, “Barirah, have you seen anything about her that makes you doubt her?” Barirah said, “No, by the One who sent you with the truth. I have seen nothing in her that I would criticize, except that she is a young girl who sometimes falls asleep while the dough of her family is unattended, and the domestic animal comes and eats it.” The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, then stood and sought someone to defend him against ‘Abd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul that day. ‘A’ishah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said from the pulpit, “O Muslims, who will defend me against a man whose harm against my household has reached me? By Allah, I know nothing but good of my household. They have also spoken of a man of whom I know nothing but good, and he never entered my household except when he was with me.” Sa‘d ibn Mu‘adh al-Ansari stood and said, “Messenger of Allah, I will defend you against him. If he is from the Aws, I will strike his neck; if he is from our brothers, the Khazraj, command us and we will carry out your command.” Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah, the leader of the Khazraj, stood. Before this he had been a righteous man, but tribal zeal seized him. He said to Sa‘d, “By Allah, you lie. You will not kill him, and you are not able to kill him.” Usayd ibn Hudayr, who was Sa‘d’s cousin, stood and said to Sa‘d ibn ‘Ubadah, “By Allah, you lie. We will kill him, for you are a hypocrite arguing on behalf of the hypocrites.” The two clans, Aws and Khazraj, became agitated and were close to fighting one another while the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, was standing on the pulpit. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, kept calming them until they fell silent, and he too became quiet. ‘A’ishah said: I spent that whole day unable to stop weeping and unable to sleep. The next morning my parents were with me. I had wept for two nights and a day, unable to sleep or stop my tears, and they thought that my weeping would split my liver. While they sat with me and I was weeping, a woman from the Ansar asked permission to enter. I gave her permission, and she sat and wept with me. While we were in that state, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, entered, greeted us, and sat down. Since the accusation had been made, he had not sat with me before then; a month had passed without revelation coming to him concerning my case. When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, sat down, he said the testimony of faith and then said, “To proceed, ‘A’ishah, I have heard such-and-such about you. If you are innocent, Allah will declare you innocent. But if you have committed a sin, then seek Allah’s forgiveness and repent to Him, for when a servant acknowledges a sin and then repents to Allah, Allah accepts his repentance.” When the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, finished speaking, my tears dried up so completely that I could not feel a single drop. I said to my father, “Answer the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, on my behalf.” He said, “By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah.” I said to my mother, “Answer the Messenger of Allah.” She said, “I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah.” I said—I was a young girl who had not memorized much of the Quran—“By Allah, I know that you have heard this talk until it settled in your hearts, and you have believed it. If I tell you that I am innocent—and Allah knows that I am innocent—you will not believe me. And if I admit to something, while Allah knows that I am innocent of it, you will believe me. By Allah, I can find no example for you except what Yusuf’s father said: ‘So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe’ (12:18).” Then I turned over and lay down on my bed. At that moment I knew that I was innocent and that Allah would declare me innocent. But, by Allah, I did not think that Allah would reveal Quran to be recited concerning my case. I considered my case too insignificant for Allah to speak about me in a revelation that would be recited. I had only hoped that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, would see a dream in which Allah would declare me innocent. By Allah, the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, had not moved from his place, nor had anyone left the household, when revelation came to him. The same distress that used to come over him seized him, until sweat poured from him like pearls, even though it was a cold day, because of the weight of the words being revealed to him. When the revelation lifted from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, he was smiling. The first words he said were, “‘A’ishah, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has declared you innocent.” My mother said, “Get up and go to him.” I said, “By Allah, I will not get up to go to him, and I will praise none but Allah, Mighty and Majestic.” Allah revealed, ‘Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you…’ (24:11), all ten verses. When Allah revealed this concerning my innocence, Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, who used to support Mistah ibn Uthathah because of their kinship and Mistah’s poverty, said, “By Allah, I will never spend anything on Mistah after what he said about ‘A’ishah.” Then Allah revealed, ‘Let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give to their relatives, the poor, and those who emigrated in the way of Allah. Let them pardon and overlook. Do you not love that Allah should forgive you? Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.’ Abu Bakr said, “Yes, by Allah, I love that Allah should forgive me.” So he resumed the support he used to give Mistah, and said, “By Allah, I will never withdraw it from him.” ‘A’ishah said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, asked Zaynab bint Jahsh about my case. He said, “Zaynab, what do you know or what have you seen?” She replied, “Messenger of Allah, I protect my hearing and my sight. I know nothing but good.” ‘A’ishah said: She was the one among the wives of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who competed with me for his favor, but Allah protected her through her piety. Her sister Hamnah began to defend her, and she perished among those who perished from the people of the slander.’”
